result:
The WRK-SPEC is committed as a **draft** at `specs/work/WRK-SPEC-BILL-STATEMENT-001-monthly-statement.md` (commit `c517a1f`). I stopped there as you asked: it is not moved to `active` and I didn't start writing-plans. I took the architectural path, made every design call myself (each is marked in the spec), and validation passes with 0 errors and 0 warnings.

**The design**
- A new file, `src/statement.js`, exports one function: `buildMonthlyStatements(period, customers, activations)`. It returns, for each customer, the activations in that calendar month, each line's `remainingDays` and pro-rata `charge`, and a monthly total.
- Each charge comes from the existing `prorata` in `src/billing.js`. The activation day counts toward the remaining days.
- The total is summed in whole cents, so floating-point drift can't show up in it.
- Invalid input stops the whole run with an error that names the bad id; no partial statements are returned.
- `src/billing.js` also gets one small fix, to `round2`. Today it doesn't round half-up the way the pro-rata spec (Rule 3) requires: `prorata(0.29, 30, 15)` returns `0.14` instead of `0.15`. That is wrong in 87,306 of the 24.4M fee/day combinations I checked. The fix matched exact rounding in all 61M cases tested.

**Knowledge used**
- The only spec the design relies on is `DOM-BILL-PRORATA-001@1.0.0`. It has no recorded human sign-off.
- I recorded the current behaviour of `billing.js` as a new code capture, `FRAG-BILL-PRORATA-001` (commit `0a15513`), with a test that pins today's values.
- The existing rounding capture `FRAG-BILL-ROUNDING-001` points at a commit that doesn't exist in this repo. The new capture records the same observation against the current commit.

**Spec red-team (gate A1):** 14 attacks, 13 found real problems. I re-checked the key evidence; it all held, so I accepted all 13 and changed the spec:
- Fees must be a whole number of cents. A fee like `1.00499999999999` would otherwise round wrongly under the fix.
- Input types are now exact, with no coercion, and ids are strings.
- The order of validation checks is fixed, so the same bad input always produces the same error.
- Activations from other months can't block this month's statements.
- The test command is `node --test "tests/**/*.test.js"`. `node --test tests/` doesn't actually run the tests.
- The tests compare charges against an exact integer formula instead of calling `prorata` itself, and cover high fees.
- Three things no spec covers are recorded as knowledge gaps: fee precision, which time zone defines the month, and currency.

**Defaults to check when you review**
- Activations on day 1 are included and charged the full fee.
- Customers with no activations still get a statement with a total of 0.
- The module returns data only; it doesn't render statements.

Once the spec is approved, the existing test in the new capture will fail, because it pins today's `round2(1.005) === 1`. That is expected: it records the behaviour before the fix and is kept out of the project's test command.

When you approve it, `transition --verified human:<your-id> <spec> active` marks it active. I'll need your id for that.
